claims.text: The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating has a nominally homogeneous solid-solution microstructure and uniform elemental distribution.
A tailored post-deposition heat treatment will enhance Cu segregation at the coating surface.
Surface segregation of Cu will promote preferential oxidation of Cu during high-temperature sliding.
Preferential oxidation of segregated Cu will form a continuous Cu-oxide surface layer.
The surface oxide layer will likely consist of CuO and/or Cu2O.
The resulting Cu-oxide layer will be adherent and lubricious.
The Cu-oxide film will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal contact will reduce adhesive wear.
Cu-oxide formation will shift subsurface deformation from dislocation-mediated plasticity toward grain-boundary-mediated deformation.
Heat-treated coatings with enhanced Cu segregation will have lower friction coefficients than untreated homogeneous coatings.
Heat-treated coatings with enhanced Cu segregation will have lower wear rates than untreated homogeneous coatings.
Heat-treated coatings with enhanced Cu segregation will exhibit less severe microscopic deformation.
Heat-treated coatings will exhibit fewer and less pronounced intergranular fractures.
Temperatures within approximately 300–600 °C can drive oxidation relevant to the proposed mechanism.
At lower temperatures, oxidation kinetics may be too slow for the proposed protective film to develop.
At excessively high temperatures, rapid oxide spallation may cause the film to lose integrity.
Oxide composition and stability vary with temperature and ambient oxygen partial pressure.
The protective capability of the proposed Cu-oxide layer varies with temperature and ambient oxygen partial pressure.
